question: Do intervention-induced changes in candidate costs exceed the native decision margins?
population: All 192 completed canonical development scenarios in the September 10 common-candidate decision diagnostic; not protected confirmation
metrics: Native winning index and second-best cost margin
Mean and centered RMS of intervention-minus-native candidate costs
Centered cost-change energy fraction (cost space, not activation coefficient space)
Largest centered pairwise cost perturbation divided by native runner-up margin
Sufficient no-flip certificate: perturbation range strictly below native runner-up margin
Exact per-candidate margin crossings relative to the native winner
Top-10 elite overlap and Spearman rank agreement
Descriptive score softmax entropy with temperature fixed to the native within-scenario population score standard deviation, shared across arms
entropy_boundary: This temperature-dependent cost-distribution diagnostic is not the entropy of the CEM sampling Gaussian or physical uncertainty.
analysis_unit: Scenario; candidate rows are not independent replicates
uncertainty: Descriptive paired scenario bootstrap, 20000 resamples, seed 2026091321, marginal 95% intervals; no new confirmatory significance claims
exclusions: Only engineering records; fail on missing scientific records, hash failures, invalid scores or unregistered arms. No exclusion by outcome.
interpretation: The common bank is the initial 300 candidates, not a full iterative CEM rollout. This analysis localizes cost/ranking changes but cannot establish the cause of protected behavioral outcomes.
